title: Stop the rules card saying "1 asks you" on a deal nothing waits on
body:
## Summary
readClauses turns clause 6 (ask me above) into the verdict "asks · your approval is needed" by arithmetic on any live deal over the threshold, even when no attention item names the clause, so the Rules card badges "1 asks you" while the answer line says nothing needs the owner.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:5-8 states the honesty rule: the only verdict taken from Rust is the clause an AttentionItem names. model.ts:207-211 (human_present_over) returns reading "asks" whenever total > amount and the deal is live, independent of ctx.asks. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/deal/DealPage.tsx:133-134 feeds that into rulesBadge, which badges the Rules card. Fixed: without ctx.asks the arithmetic reading is a forward fact with a non-asking state, and only ctx.asks yields "asks". Also covers post-approval live states (APPROVED/SETTLING) where decided_by is human and the rule still reads "your approval is needed".

## Flow
- open the house seller haggle D-0204 (NEGOTIATING, $312 > $250, no attention item)
- Rules card value reads "1 asks you"; the answer line reads "... Nothing needs you right now."
- fix: human_present_over without ctx.asks returns a non-asking reading; update the model.test.ts by(6) and story.test.ts rulesBadge expectations

## Expected impact
An owner no longer sees a gold "asks you" badge on a deal that asks nothing. Could break: model/story tests that pin by(6)==="asks" without ctx (they pin the old expression; strengthen them).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the Rules card agrees with the decision area
Before: probe over the mock world (20 deals): 1 live deal (D-0204) reads clause 6 "asks" with no attention item
After: not measured - the gate needs the semantics changed across model.test.ts and story.test.ts
Method: probe - readClauses over buildMockState; the gate rung needs an M change with risk 4
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:5
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:207
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/deal/DealPage.tsx:133
probe: D-0204 NEGOTIATING decided_by:- attn:no-item -> asks "$312.00 > $250.00 · your approval is needed"
instrument: model.test.ts: readClauses(clausesOf(D-0204), D-0204) with no ctx.asks must not read clause 6 as "asks"; story.test.ts: rulesBadge(ruleChecks(...)) for D-0204 is null; D-0193 with asks:6 still "asks"

title: Word one authority the same in the answer line and in "Who decided"
body:
## Summary
The deal page names who decided twice, from two Rust records with two vocabularies: the answer line reads Deal.decided_by through logic.decidedBy, the story view reads HistoryStep.authority through logic.whoDecided, and three of five authorities are worded differently.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/logic.ts:227-237 (decidedBy): policy -> "your rule · <rule>", house_mandate -> "house seller rules", safe_default -> "the deadline". logic.ts:724-735 (whoDecided): signed_rule -> "Your rules", house_mandate -> "The house seller’s rules", safe_default -> "The safe default". apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/story.ts:115-116 shows the first ("decided by the deadline"); apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/deal/decided.ts:16-20 the second ("The safe default · no PayPal call"), on the same story view. Fixed: one word table keyed by authority kind that both functions read.

## Flow
- open a lapsed deal (D-0184): answer sub "... · decided by the deadline"; Who decided row "The safe default · no PayPal call"
- fix: a shared authority word table in logic.ts used by decidedBy and whoDecided

## Expected impact
The owner reads one name for one decider across the page. Could break: deadlineEnds.test.tsx pins "The safe default ·".

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one vocabulary per authority
Before: 3 of 5 authority kinds worded differently between the two functions
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - three cases walked (policy D-0192, safe_default D-0184, house_mandate); logic.ts is outside this round’s paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: logic.test.ts: for every DecidedBy variant and its HistoryAuthority counterpart, decidedBy(..).text and whoDecided(..) share one lead word; deadlineEnds.test.tsx still green

title: Fold the deal page strip tables into the ones logic.ts already has
body:
## Summary
deal/model.ts keeps byte-identical copies of logic.ts’s SETTLED, OFF and BRANCH_AFTER tables, and mirrorStrip re-implements stripFor’s terminal-prefix walk, so a new terminal state must be added in two places that nothing checks agree.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:29-32 vs apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/logic.ts:54,57,135 (git grep BRANCH_AFTER: 2 definitions, identical text; model.ts:31 says "mirrors logic.ts"). mirrorStrip (model.ts:50-78) and stripFor (logic.ts:143-160, used by console/areas/counter/Order.tsx) both walk BRANCH_AFTER. Fixed: logic.ts exports the three tables, model.ts imports them, and a test diffs the two strips per state.

## Flow
- export SETTLED, OFF, BRANCH_AFTER from logic.ts
- delete the model.ts copies and import them
- add a parity test over every DealState x kind x side

## Expected impact
Developers add a terminal state once. Could break: nothing at runtime; an import change plus a guard.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the strip tables
Before: 3 tables defined twice (6 definitions), 0 tests that the two strips agree
After: 3 definitions, 1 parity test (predicted)
Method: simulation - the export touches logic.ts, outside this round’s paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: new parity test: for each DealState x kind x side, mirrorStrip(d) done/todo statuses equal stripFor(d) minus its appended terminal step; seed red by editing one BRANCH_AFTER copy

title: Project Rust’s per-clause gate verdicts to the Main window
body:
## Summary
The "Rules that applied" view reconstructs each clause verdict by client arithmetic (or "unknown") because Rust does not project its per-clause gate results to Main; each reading is a second implementation of the gate that can disagree with it.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:5-8 records the decision; model.ts:174-224 re-derives roles, pinned/house counterparties, per-deal limit, band and threshold, and marks velocity, payees and lever unknown. The clause-6 card in this file is one measured disagreement. Fixed: a read-tier IPC field carrying Rust’s verdict per clause for a deal, which readClauses displays instead of computing.

## Flow
- add a per-clause verdict projection (deal_display or a new read command: authority table row, bindings, PINNED_MANIFEST)
- readClauses shows it; arithmetic stays only as a labelled fallback

## Expected impact
The owner sees the gate’s own verdicts. Could break: the IPC contract and its pinned manifest.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for clause verdicts
Before: 9 clause kinds, 5 computed client-side, 4 unknown or not-applicable
After: 9 from Rust (predicted)
Method: simulation - a contract change, not buildable in a client round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
